parallel-programming-with-openmp.title: Parallel programming with OpenMP
parallel-programming-with-openmp.goal: Exam-grade understanding: look at C code and decide whether and how to parallelize it with OpenMP, and explain the benefits and limitations. Scope: core + tasks + extras (SIMD, nested parallelism, memory model/flush). Env: gcc 13.3, 8 hw threads.
edge: concurrency fundamentals: floor = shared address space, race via load/add/store interleave, false sharing = perf not correctness, Amdahl 1/s, default-shared scoping of outer vars; ceiling = none found here (solid)

OpenMP construct semantics: floor = parallel runs block once per thread, unordered; ceiling = does not know static vs dynamic schedule, reduction identity init, which constructs have implicit barriers (master), believes tasks spawn a new thread each (thread pool/team model missing)

nodes.label: All threads in a team share one address space; only variables on a thread's own stack are its own
nodes.summary: declaration location -> instance count landed on 2nd try; C gap: reads r=q as 'r points to q' (confuses copying a pointer's value with &q); revisit explicitly in n6 (private pointer, shared pointee)

nodes.label: Data race (same location, >=1 write, no ordering) is undefined behaviour; correct = race-free
nodes.why: the correctness criterion everything is checked against; learner holds 'wrong result', not yet 'UB'
nodes.summary: after correction: race -> UB independent of optimization level; correctness = race-free source (re-check 4/5)

nodes.label: Fork-join: parallel creates one team; every other construct only divides work among that team
nodes.why: root that fixes the 'task = new thread' misconception
nodes.summary: fork-join landed: tasks run on existing team (5/5); after demo, parallel replicates vs omp for divides (re-check 5/5)

nodes.label: A loop is parallelizable iff its iterations are independent (no loop-carried dependence)
nodes.why: derived: concurrent iterations in any order + race rule
nodes.summary: derivation 3/5 (rule lacked 'different iterations'); after precise rule, classified 3 loops correctly (a[i]+=1 safe, a[i+1] anti-dep, shared scalar write) 5/5 each

nodes.label: omp for / parallel for divides iterations; implicit barrier at end; nowait
nodes.summary: derived implicit barrier between dependent loops (4/5); nowait check 5/5; static same-assignment rule for nowait introduced, revisit in n9

nodes.label: Data scoping: shared, private, firstprivate, lastprivate, default rules, default(none)
Synchronization: barrier, critical, atomic, single vs master/masked (no barrier)
Reductions: private copy at identity, combine at end; why only associative ops
Scheduling: static, dynamic, guided, chunk size; load imbalance
Performance model: Amdahl, fork/join and sync overhead, false sharing, memory bandwidth
Tasks: work units queued for the team; task, taskwait, taskgroup, task data scoping
Memory model: why threads can see stale values; flush and implied flushes
SIMD: vector parallelism inside one thread; omp simd, parallel for simd
GOAL: read code and decide if and how to parallelize, with benefits and limitations
